question: Is the WFE turn-cap loop a harness/template/setting fault or a model fault?
setup: identical minimal multi-turn tool loop (file_read packet.json -> answer; the packet contains the answer) on two engines: Ollama 0.40.0 (Ollama parser + GGUF-embedded official template) and brew llama-server 9950/961e4b26a --jinja (llama.cpp parser + same embedded template). Sampling = auto-compliance lane policy (0.3/0.95/20/0/rep 1.1), think off.
harness_checks_cleared: render parity 5/5 (all five shapes incl. tool round-trip) on both Ollama tags against the official template — p1_render_*.json
sampling keys delivered (engine_contract_check PASS on Ollama 0.40.0, 2026-10-11; targets /v1)
think:false honored on /v1 (contract check think:false delivered, reasoning absent)
tool calls executed 160/160 without error in the WFE runs; no bad-args feedback
the WFE debug transcripts show the model received its own prior calls and results (it derived the governing_ref string it later hunts for, from the packet it just read)

system_prompt_WITH 'Answer with JSON: {d.ollama_T32: looped all 6 turns: file_read of hallucinated CIP-009-6_R1_Part_4.1.{md,txt,pdf,docx,html}
system_prompt_WITH 'Answer with JSON: {d.llama_server_jinja: looped 5/5 seeds (7-11): same hallucinated-filename hunt, e.g. file_read CIP-009-6_R1_Part_4.1.md
system_prompt_WITH 'Answer with JSON: {d.note: the hunted string exists only INSIDE packet.json — proof the tool result reached the model

system_prompt_WITHOUT the JSON clause.llama_server_jinja: ANSWERED 10/10 across seeds (7-11) and max_tokens (256/4096), both sampling variants

verdict: MODEL fault, not harness: the loop reproduces on stock llama.cpp with Saluki's own embedded template and parser under an output-format instruction + tools; templates render identically; sampling and think control verified delivered; tool execution clean. A 2-bit instruction-following collapse under tool-calling. Mitigation (drop explicit format clauses when tools are offered) is integration work behind the operator gate.
